g15.basis: ADR-0021 + comet-ai-devops-convergence.md: under normal dependencies discovery <=3 minutes and isolation <=2 minutes; fault exposure, alert delivery and isolation are timed separately from real timestamps, and an alert never counts as isolation. Fault-window breaches are recorded (exposure window/breach), never hidden by a timeout.
g15.evidenceNote: the targets and the separate-timing rule are registered here; production timing evidence from a real deployment (real external timestamps per segment) is still to be supplied and stays UNVERIFIED.

r10.basis: R10: an unresolved Run/knowledge obligation retains the sole workspace and blocks cleanup; the monitor observes unresolved obligations and their deadlines and alerts on them — it never performs, triggers or substitutes cleanup.
r10.note: cleanup eligibility evidence belongs to I08 (retention/restore policies); this registration only pins the monitor's observe-and-alert role.

negativeRedLines.note: revision 2026-10-26-comet-050-adoption-v1 red lines: a missed required alert (missed event / stalled watermark / offline / isolation failure) is itself a failure, never a silent pass; an alert never substitutes isolation — isolation executes and reads back only through the original Comet maintenance entry; offline is detectable only from outside the fault domain (fault-domain-policy.json); compensation for any of these events belongs to the original Comet, never to the monitor or the scheduler.
